title: Fondant Potatoes (Butter-Basted Potato Cylinders)
summary: Thick potato cylinders are seared until deeply golden, then slowly basted and braised in butter, garlic and stock until the inside turns almost custard-soft. The reduced pan juices make the perfect finishing sauce.
equipment: large ovenproof frying pan (30 cm), stainless or cast iron

ingredients.item: large waxy or all-purpose potatoes (such as Yukon Gold), peeled
fine sea salt or table salt
chicken stock or vegetable stock, low-salt

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) at least 20 minutes ahead, so the potatoes finish cooking in a fully heated oven rather than one still warming up.

steps.title: Shape the potatoes
steps.text: Trim the peeled potatoes into 4-5cm tall cylinders with flat top and bottom; a round cutter about 5cm across makes this quick and keeps every piece the same size. Even cylinders cook and brown at the same rate, so none finish before the others.

steps.title: Dry and season
steps.text: Pat the potatoes completely dry, then season all over with the salt and pepper. A dry surface browns properly in the hot oil — any surface moisture would simply steam instead of sear.

steps.title: Sear the first side
steps.text: Heat the oil in the ovenproof pan over medium-high until shimmering, then stand the potatoes on one flat end and sear without moving for 5-7 minutes until deep golden. Resist checking them too soon — moving them early stops a proper crust forming.

steps.title: Sear the other side
steps.text: Turn the potatoes onto the other flat end and sear for a further 4-5 minutes until that side is equally golden.

steps.title: Baste in butter
steps.text: Lower the heat to medium and add the butter, garlic and thyme to the pan. As soon as the butter foams, spoon it over the potatoes for 1-2 minutes so the aromatics flavour every side.

steps.title: Add stock and transfer to the oven
steps.text: Pour in the stock so it comes halfway up the potatoes, then move the pan to the oven. Cook for 25-35 minutes, basting twice, until a knife slides through with no resistance and the liquid has reduced to a glossy glaze. The potatoes slowly absorb the buttery stock as it simmers, which is what makes the inside meltingly soft.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Lift the potatoes out and spoon the glossy pan juices over the top before serving.

tips: Dry the potato cylinders properly before searing — any surface moisture will steam instead of brown and you'll end up with a pale crust.
Don't move the potatoes while they're searing; disturbing them too early is the most common reason the crust fails to form.
Cut the cylinders to an even size so they all finish cooking in the same time.
Baste regularly once the stock goes in — it keeps the top from drying out while the inside softens.
storage: Best served straight from the pan, but leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a covered pan with a splash of stock or water until piping hot throughout. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
